title: The Midtown Moose
logline: Fed up with Sandy Rivers stealing her stories, Robin plants a fake exclusive about a moose loose in Midtown, sure he'll humiliate himself on air. Instead the moose comes true, because Ted, Marshall, Lily and Barney each secretly need Gary to exist, and they all turn up to stop Robin from confessing on Sandy's live special.
coldOpen: Kids, every reporter dreams of breaking a story so big the whole city talks about it. Your Aunt Robin did it once. The trick was, she made it up.

guests.name: Dr. Fern Ostrander
guests.role: a Montana wildlife biologist who flies in to track the moose; blunt, unromantic, answers every flirtation with a moose fact, and can read a track like a fingerprint

guests.name: Delia
guests.role: a woman at MacLaren's who finds each new detail of Barney's moose sighting more irresistible than the last

scenes.summary: Sandy steals Robin's ferry-wedding exclusive live on air. During the break Robin fakes a whispered phone call about a moose loose in Midtown named Gary who only eats everything bagels. Sandy grabs it and opens the next segment with it. Robin is delighted.

beats.line: Sandy Rivers sat next to Robin for six years. In that time, he broke two hundred stories. All of them hers.
Tonight, a Metro News One exclusive. For eleven years, a Staten Island Ferry captain has been secretly—
Running a wedding chapel in the engine room. Two hundred weddings. Zero licenses.
I'm Sandy Rivers. You heard it here first.
That's my story. I rode that ferry for three weeks.
And it shows. You smell like a diesel wedding.
After the break: is your cat plotting against you? Sources say yes.
Third one this month, Sandy. You read my notes upside down from across the desk.
I'm a trained journalist, Robin. I can read upside down, sideways and through a manila envelope.
You're not a journalist. You're a very handsome photocopier.
Very handsome.
Hi. It's Robin. Is it confirmed? A full-grown bull moose? Loose in Midtown?
Eating out of bagel carts. But only everything bagels. Wow.
And Parks named him Gary. Okay. I'll break it tomorrow. Nobody else can know.
Who was that?
Nobody. A source. A Canadian source. About Canadian animals. Mind your business.
Robin, I'll take the top of the segment.
Oh, no. Please don't.
Breaking news. A moose is loose in Midtown.
A twelve-hundred-pound bull named Gary. He eats only everything bagels. Bagel carts are terrified.
And only one anchor in New York had the courage to tell you. Me.
Enjoy it, Sandy. By lunch tomorrow, you're the man who reported a moose.
It was a perfect plan. It lasted nineteen hours.

scenes.summary: Four days later the moose is everywhere and Sandy is on the side of a bus. Robin interrogates the gang: Lily has been writing letters from Gary to her kindergarten (and using him for discipline), Barney claims to have seen him (cutaway), Marshall used him to win a three-year habitat case, and Ted faked the hoofprints in his cowboy boots to keep a moose biologist in town. Robin vows to confess on Sandy's live special. Fern arrives: she's booked on the special too, and she'll find whoever faked the tracks.

beats.line: Four days later, Gary the moose was the biggest story in New York.
Hoofprints on the Great Lawn. An emergency court order. Forty letters from a moose to a kindergarten.
And a man at a bar who says he looked Gary in the eye.
Sandy Rivers is on the side of a bus. Hugging a cartoon moose like a prom date.
I know! What a week for Gary!
There is no Gary! I named him after my orthodontist!
I told every one of you it was fake. Right here. At this table.
You did. You did a little victory dance. It was mostly shoulders.
So which one of you is it?
Okay, it was me, but it was for the children!
You wrote forty letters as a moose?
They wrote to him first, Robin. Twenty little crayon letters. Tyler drew him a hat.
Also, Gary sees everything. And Gary does not like biting.
Four days. Zero biters. Nap time ran forty minutes over. Nobody moved a muscle.
She's running a kindergarten on fear of an imaginary moose. I've never loved her more.
And the man at the bar.
I may have casually mentioned to one woman that I'd seen him. Once. In passing.
Three a.m. Fifth Avenue. Steam rising off the street. And there he was.
Gary?
Our eyes met. Two alphas. He nodded, as if to say: you take Manhattan, I'll take the Bronx.
Weren't you scared?
He was eating an everything bagel. He offered me half. I took it. You don't say no to Gary.
I have never wanted anyone more.
Once. In passing.
Eleven times. Eleven women. Gary is the best wingman I've ever had.
Sorry, buddy. You've been replaced by an animal that doesn't exist.
I made up the bagel, Barney.
And it's my best material. Thank you.
Marshall. Please tell me you are not the court order.
That empty lot on 51st Street. Three years I've been fighting to keep a parking garage off it. No judge would listen.
Then I put the word moose in the first sentence. Judge Pell wept, Robin.
Emergency wildlife habitat. The first environmental case I've ever won.
For a moose who does not exist.
The airplane didn't exist until somebody made it up. Bigfoot is on the same journey. Just slower.
Ted. You're awfully quiet. And you're wearing cowboy boots.
Fine! Her name is Fern. She's a moose biologist from Montana. She flies home tomorrow unless there's fresh sign!
She told me a bull moose will walk forty miles for a mate. Robin, she was flirting.
So you walked across the Great Lawn. In what?
My boots. Heel first. Backwards. A cowboy heel is basically a cloven hoof, if you believe in yourself.
Dad. You faked a moose to get a girlfriend.
I didn't fake a moose, Luke. I supported a moose.
Sandy's doing a live special tomorrow night. Moose Hunter. And at the top of the hour, I'm telling the whole city I made it up.
No!
I'm a journalist. And Sandy Rivers does not get to keep my moose.
Fern! Hi! These are my friends.
Moose don't have friends. That's how they stay alive.
Good news. Sandy Rivers booked me for his special. If the moose is real, I'll find him.
And if somebody faked those tracks, I'll find them too.
Great. That's great. Both of those are great.

scenes.summary: On her way up to confess, Robin gets stuck in the elevator with Sandy. Sandy can't drop the broadcast voice and claims credit for pressing the alarm. He reveals he knew the moose was fake from day one and ran it because her stories are always good. Robin explains why credit matters: her dad cheered every goal with 'That's my boy', and her name under a story was the first time anybody got her right. Sandy asks if he can use it.

beats.line: Good evening. I'm Robin Scherbatsky, and there is no moose.
Good evening. I lied to Sandy Rivers. Which, honestly, should count as a public service.
Robin. Big night. My big night. You're also in it.
Did we just stop?
Breaking news. We are stuck between floors.
You don't have to do the voice, Sandy. It's just us.
Robin, I haven't used my real voice since 1987. I don't know where it went.
Just press the alarm.
We should press the alarm. You heard it here first.
I said that. Four seconds ago.
And now it's on the record.
Sandy, when these doors open, I'm going on air and telling everyone the moose is fake.
I know it's fake.
Since when?
Since you whispered it into a phone you were holding upside down.
Then why did you run it?
Because it was a great story. Yours always are, Robin. Why do you think I take them?
That's almost a compliment.
Don't let it go to your head. I'm a thief, not a mentor.
Why do you even care? It's a name at the bottom of the screen. Nobody reads the bottom.
My dad wanted a son. So every time I scored a goal, he'd stand up in the bleachers and yell, that's my boy.
Every goal. For ten years. That's my boy.
The first time I saw Robin Scherbatsky under a story I broke, it was the first time anybody got me right.
It was never about beating you. I just want the name at the bottom to be mine.
Robin. That's beautiful.
Can I use it?
No.
For my memoir. I'd change the sport. Polo.
We're moving.
Do what you have to do tonight. But fix your hair. It's my special.

scenes.summary: Moose Hunter, live. Barney testifies, Fern identifies the hoofprints as a size eleven cowboy boot and Ted corrects her to ten and a half. Robin starts to confess; Marshall and Lily burst in to stop her. As she tries again, Sandy cuts in and credits her with the story on air, then adds that if it's fake, it's on her. Robin keeps her friends' moose alive under her own name. Fern reveals a real hoofprint and a half-eaten everything bagel at the lot. Nobody planted it.

beats.line: Good evening. I'm Sandy Rivers, and this is Moose Hunter: The Sandy Rivers Story.
Joining me, our eyewitness. Barney Stinson.
Thank you, Sandy. Ladies of the tri-state area: I'm single, and I have split a bagel with a moose.
And from Montana Fish and Wildlife, Doctor Fern Ostrander.
Eleven years studying moose. I've never seen one in a city. I've never been on television. I don't care for either.
Doctor. The tracks on the Great Lawn.
Deep. Cloven. Pressed heel first, which no moose in history has ever done.
In my professional opinion, they were made by a size eleven cowboy boot.
Ten and a half.
Ted.
The heel runs big.
Okay. Our viewers deserve the truth.
Robin, wait!
The bulldozers come Monday. Gary is all that's standing between that lot and a parking garage.
Robin. Twenty kindergarteners are watching this. And so is Gary.
And I have a date at nine with a woman who thinks I arm-wrestled him. And won.
There is no—
No question about who broke this story. And it wasn't me.
This story came from my colleague, Robin Scherbatsky. You heard it from her first.
Sandy.
So if it turns out to be fake, that's on her.
Fine. It's my story. And there is no doubt in my mind. Gary is out there.
She's right. At six this morning, on the lot on 51st Street, I found a fresh print. A real hoof.
Right next to it, half an everything bagel.
Who did that?
Not me.
Gary.
Marshall. What did you have for breakfast?
Oatmeal. Everything oatmeal. It's a Minnesota thing.
Kids, nobody ever found Gary. But that lot on 51st Street is still the only moose habitat in Manhattan.
The plaque says, discovered by Robin Scherbatsky. Underneath, in bigger letters: as first reported by Sandy Rivers.
